claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr undergoes rapid oxidation or pesting in air under conditions similar to 800 °C for 5 hours.
A thin aluminide coating can be deposited on equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr by pack cementation.
The aluminide coating will form a continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale during exposure to air at approximately 800 °C.
The resulting alumina scale will be stable and self-healing.
Alumina is thermodynamically stable and slow-growing under the proposed high-temperature oxidation conditions.
The alumina scale will passivate the surface and reduce oxygen diffusion into the bulk alloy.
The coating will leave the bulk alloy microstructure largely unaffected.
Leaving the bulk microstructure largely unaffected will preserve the alloy's bulk mechanical properties.
Relative to untreated material, the coated alloy will show significantly less oxide-scale growth and pesting after 5 hours in air at 800 °C.
The coated alloy will retain its room-temperature tensile ductility after coating and oxidation exposure.
The coated alloy will retain its high-temperature yield strength around 1000 °C after coating and oxidation exposure.
The proposed protection is applicable in atmospheric air near 800 °C for exposures on the order of 5 hours under minimal mechanical load.
The coating should not compromise mechanical performance from room temperature to 1000 °C under the previously reported low-strain-rate loading conditions.
Similar refractory alloys have benefited from aluminide coatings for oxidation resistance.
Coating thickness, uniformity, and post-process heat treatment may affect performance and require optimization for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating process may introduce defects or residual stresses that degrade mechanical performance.
